title: Intermittent evening disconnections on broadband
body:
Drops that occur at the same time each evening usually point to peak-hour congestion or an unstable line profile on the local cabinet rather than a fault inside the home. Check the line statistics for a falling signal-to-noise margin at peak time and for high error counts. If the margin falls below 6 dB in the evening, apply the stable line profile and arrange a monitored line test over 72 hours. Customers who have already power-cycled the router should not be asked to repeat it.

  1. Check line statistics in the diagnostics portal for SNR margin and error counts during the evening window.
  2. If the margin drops below 6 dB at peak time, apply the stable line profile to the connection.
  3. Run a 72-hour monitored line test and ask the customer to note the time of each drop.
  4. If drops continue after the profile change, book an engineer visit to inspect the cabinet and wiring.
  5. Do not ask the customer to repeat router restarts that they have already tried.

title: Broadband drops at random times with line noise
body:
Random disconnections at all hours, often with crackling or hissing on the landline or visibly loose sockets, indicate a physical line fault: a faulty microfilter, damaged internal wiring or a poor joint outside. Test with the master socket and a replacement microfilter before escalating to an engineer.

  1. Ask the customer to plug the router into the master socket with a new microfilter and no extension cables.
  2. Run a remote line test and check for noise, crosstalk and high error counts.
  3. If the line test shows a fault, raise a fault ticket with the line repair team.
  4. Book an engineer visit and give the customer the appointment window.
  5. Advise that no charge applies when the fault is on the provider's network.

If the line test shows a fault, raise a fault ticket with the line repair team.
Book an engineer visit and give the customer the appointment window.

title: Wi-Fi disconnects while wired connection is stable
body:
If devices lose Wi-Fi but a laptop on an Ethernet cable stays online, the broadband line is healthy and the fault is in the wireless layer. Common causes are channel congestion from neighbouring networks, outdated router firmware or devices stuck on a weak 2.4 GHz band.

  1. Confirm the wired connection stays online while Wi-Fi drops to isolate the fault to the wireless layer.
  2. Change the Wi-Fi channel to a less crowded one (1, 6 or 11 on 2.4 GHz) and enable automatic channel selection.
  3. Update the router firmware to the latest version.
  4. Enable band steering or a separate 5 GHz network for devices that support it.
  5. If the problem persists, replace the router with a newer model.

title: Slow broadband speeds during peak hours
body:
Speeds that are normal in the morning but slow in the evening are usually caused by contention on the local network or a speed profile reduced after repeated line errors. Run a wired speed test at two times of day, compare against the minimum guaranteed speed in the contract, and check whether the line profile was automatically capped.

  1. Ask the customer to run a wired speed test in the morning and again in the evening and record both results.
  2. Compare the results against the minimum guaranteed speed in the customer's contract.
  3. Check whether the line profile has been automatically capped after errors and reset the profile if so.
  4. If the evening speed stays below the guaranteed minimum, log a speed fault and escalate for network capacity review.
  5. Offer the customer a service credit if the guaranteed minimum is not met.

title: Weak Wi-Fi signal in distant rooms
body:
Poor speed only in far rooms or upstairs, with full speed next to the router, is a coverage problem and not a line problem. Move the router to a central, elevated spot, use the 5 GHz band for nearby devices, and add a mesh extender or powerline adapter for far rooms.

  1. Run a speed test next to the router to confirm the line delivers full speed.
  2. Move the router to a central, elevated position away from walls, microwaves and cordless phones.
  3. Use the 5 GHz band for devices close to the router and 2.4 GHz for far rooms.
  4. Recommend a mesh Wi-Fi extender or powerline adapter for rooms that remain weak.
  5. Offer the customer the Wi-Fi extender add-on from the equipment catalogue.

title: Slow mobile data speeds
body:
Slow mobile data can be due to fair-usage throttling after the monthly allowance, network congestion at a busy tower, or incorrect network settings. Check the allowance usage first, then signal quality, then reset network settings and the APN.

  1. Check whether the customer has exceeded the fair-usage data allowance and is being throttled.
  2. Check signal strength and network mode; ask the customer to switch between 4G and 5G.
  3. Reset network settings and confirm the APN settings match the provider's standard values.
  4. If speed is still low, log a congestion report for the tower location and time.
  5. Offer to add a data booster if throttling is due to the allowance.

title: Router shows red or blinking broadband light
body:
A blinking or red broadband/DSL light means the router cannot establish a line connection. Check cables and microfilters, power-cycle the router for 30 seconds, and test with a spare router. If the light stays red after these checks and the line test is healthy, the router is faulty and should be replaced.

  1. Check that the broadband cable is firmly connected and not damaged and that a microfilter is fitted.
  2. Power off the router for 30 seconds and switch it on again.
  3. Run a remote line test to confirm the line is healthy.
  4. If the line is healthy but the light stays red, send a replacement router.
  5. If the line test fails, raise a line fault ticket instead.

Power off the router for 30 seconds and switch it on again.

title: Router restarts by itself repeatedly
body:
A router that reboots on its own is usually caused by a failing power adapter, overheating, or a corrupted firmware update. Check the original power supply is used and ventilation is clear, then apply a factory reset. If it still reboots, replace the unit.

  1. Confirm the customer is using the original power adapter and the router is not covered or overheating.
  2. Perform a factory reset using the reset button for 10 seconds.
  3. Re-apply the standard configuration and update the firmware.
  4. If the router still reboots, send a replacement unit with a prepaid return label.

title: Duplicate charge on monthly bill
body:
When a customer reports being charged twice, verify the payment ledger for two successful transactions with the same amount within 48 hours. Duplicate card authorisations that are not settled drop off automatically within 5 working days, whereas settled duplicates are refunded to the original payment method within 5 to 7 working days.

  1. Open the payment ledger and look for two transactions of the same amount within 48 hours.
  2. Check whether the second transaction is only a pending authorisation or a settled payment.
  3. If the duplicate is settled, raise a refund to the original payment method.
  4. Tell the customer the refund takes 5 to 7 working days and confirm by email.
  5. If it is only a pending authorisation, explain it will drop off automatically within 5 working days.

title: Bill higher than expected after promotion ends
body:
A bill that suddenly rises is most often caused by the end of an introductory promotion, a pro-rata first bill covering part-months, or paid add-ons. Explain each line item, and where the promotion ended without notice, offer a loyalty retention discount or move the customer to a plan matching the old price.

  1. Open the bill and compare the current invoice with the previous one line by line.
  2. Identify whether the promotional discount expired, a pro-rata charge applies, or add-ons were added.
  3. Explain each changed line item to the customer in plain terms.
  4. If the customer was not notified that the promotion ended, apply a one-time goodwill credit.
  5. Offer a retention plan that matches the previous monthly price.

title: Late payment fee applied despite on-time payment
body:
If a late fee is charged although the customer paid on time, check the payment allocation date. Payments made after the cutoff or through banks with processing delays can be allocated late. Waive the first late fee when proof of payment is provided.

  1. Ask the customer for the date and method of payment, and a bank reference if available.
  2. Check the payment allocation date in the ledger against the due date.
  3. If the payment was made on time but allocated late, remove the late fee.
  4. Waive the fee as a one-time courtesy if the delay was caused by bank processing.
  5. Confirm the corrected balance to the customer in writing.

title: Charged after cancelling the service
body:
Charges that continue after cancellation are valid only until the end of the notice period. Verify the cancellation request date and the disconnection date. Billing after the effective termination date is an error and must be reversed with a refund of the post-termination charges.

  1. Look up the cancellation request date and the effective disconnection date in the account history.
  2. Check any charges dated after the effective termination date.
  3. Reverse charges applied after the termination date and process a refund.
  4. Confirm the final bill with the customer and send a cancellation confirmation by email.
  5. If the cancellation request was not recorded, escalate to the retention team to backdate it.

title: Upgrading to a faster broadband or fibre plan
body:
Customers can upgrade to a higher-speed plan at any time. Check fibre availability for the address, confirm the new monthly price and whether a new contract term starts, and schedule the change. Upgrades to a plan on the same technology take effect within 24 hours with no engineer visit.

  1. Verify the customer's address for fibre or higher-speed availability.
  2. Present the available plans with monthly price and contract length.
  3. Confirm whether a new minimum term applies and obtain the customer's agreement.
  4. Submit the upgrade order; same-technology upgrades take effect within 24 hours.
  5. Advise the customer to restart the router after the upgrade takes effect.

Present the available plans with monthly price and contract length.

title: Downgrading to a cheaper plan within contract
body:
Customers inside the minimum term who want a cheaper plan can downgrade after the minimum term, or earlier by paying an early change fee equal to the remaining discount. Check the minimum term end date, calculate the fee, and offer a retention plan before processing.

  1. Check the contract end date and whether the customer is inside the minimum term.
  2. Calculate any early change fee and explain it clearly.
  3. Offer a lower-priced retention plan that avoids the fee.
  4. If the customer still wants to downgrade, process the change effective from the next billing date.
  5. Send written confirmation of the new price and any fee.

title: No service after SIM replacement or activation
body:
A new or replaced SIM that shows 'No service' or 'Emergency calls only' usually has not finished activation, or the old SIM is still linked to the number. Confirm the SIM serial number is mapped to the line, trigger a re-provisioning, and ask the customer to restart the phone and toggle airplane mode. Re-check APN settings if data fails.

  1. Confirm the new SIM serial number is linked to the customer's mobile number.
  2. Trigger a SIM re-provisioning from the provisioning console.
  3. Ask the customer to power the phone off for one minute and then on again, and toggle airplane mode.
  4. Verify APN settings if calls work but mobile data does not.
  5. If the SIM still shows no service after 30 minutes, send a replacement SIM.

title: Poor indoor mobile coverage
body:
Weak indoor signal is common in buildings with thick walls or metal cladding. Check the coverage map and tower status. Enable Wi-Fi Calling to route calls over broadband, and offer a signal booster or femtocell if coverage at the address is confirmed as marginal.

  1. Check the coverage map and known tower issues for the customer's postcode.
  2. Enable Wi-Fi Calling and VoLTE on the customer's handset to route calls over home broadband.
  3. Ask the customer to test near a window versus inside to confirm indoor attenuation.
  4. Offer a signal booster or femtocell if the coverage is marginal.
  5. Log a coverage complaint for the radio planning team with the address.

title: Unable to make calls or send SMS but data works
body:
If data works but calls or texts fail, check whether the line has outgoing barring, an unpaid balance restriction, wrong SMS centre number or VoLTE provisioning problems. Verify the line status in the provisioning console and remove any barring after payment confirmation.

  1. Check the line status for outgoing call or SMS barring.
  2. Check whether an unpaid balance restriction was applied and, if so, confirm payment.
  3. Verify the SMS service centre number in the phone settings.
  4. Re-provision VoLTE on the line and ask the customer to restart the handset.
  5. If the issue persists, escalate to mobile core support with the IMSI.

title: Cannot log in to the customer portal or app
body:
Login failures are usually wrong credentials, an account locked after five failed attempts, or a stale session. Unlock the account after verifying identity with security questions, send a password reset link to the registered email, and ask the customer to clear the cache or use a private window.

  1. Verify the customer's identity with the security questions before changing anything.
  2. Check if the account is locked after five failed attempts and unlock it.
  3. Send a password reset link to the registered email address.
  4. Ask the customer to clear the browser cache or try a private window or the mobile app.
  5. If the reset email does not arrive, update the contact email after identity verification.

Send a password reset link to the registered email address.

title: One-time passcode (OTP) not received
body:
When the verification code does not arrive, check that the registered mobile number is correct, that the SMS is not blocked by a do-not-disturb setting, and that the OTP limit has not been hit. Resend after five minutes, or offer email or authenticator verification.

  1. Confirm the registered mobile number on the account is correct.
  2. Check whether the number has do-not-disturb or SMS-blocking enabled.
  3. Check the OTP attempt counter and wait five minutes if the limit was reached.
  4. Offer verification by email or authenticator app instead.
  5. Update the mobile number after strong identity verification if it is outdated.

Check whether the number has do-not-disturb or SMS-blocking enabled.

title: Suspected account takeover or unauthorized changes
body:
If a customer reports changes they did not make, such as a new SIM, changed email or unknown orders, treat it as a possible account takeover. Immediately lock the account, revoke active sessions, require identity verification through a secure channel, and escalate to the fraud and security team. Do not read back personal details.

  1. Lock the account and revoke all active sessions immediately.
  2. Verify the customer's identity through a secure channel without reading back personal details.
  3. Review recent changes such as SIM swaps, email changes and new orders and reverse unauthorised ones.
  4. Escalate to the fraud and security team and raise an incident ticket.
  5. Advise the customer to change passwords and enable two-factor authentication.

title: Area-wide broadband outage
body:
When several customers in the same area report no internet simultaneously, check the network status page for a known incident in that postcode. Confirm the incident reference and the estimated restoration time, tell the customer no individual fault needs to be raised, and offer an automatic outage credit once the incident exceeds 24 hours.

  1. Check the network status dashboard for an open incident covering the customer's postcode.
  2. Give the customer the incident reference and the estimated restoration time.
  3. Do not raise an individual fault ticket for a known area incident.
  4. Offer the customer SMS updates on progress of the incident.
  5. Apply the automatic outage credit if the incident lasts more than 24 hours.

title: Mobile network outage at a cell tower
body:
If many customers in one location report no mobile coverage, the serving tower may be down. Check the tower status and planned maintenance. Provide the estimated restoration time, advise enabling Wi-Fi Calling meanwhile, and apply the network outage credit for extended downtime.

  1. Check the tower status page for outages or planned maintenance at the customer's location.
  2. Provide the incident reference and estimated restoration time.
  3. Advise the customer to use Wi-Fi Calling and messaging apps over Wi-Fi in the meantime.
  4. Apply the network outage credit if the outage exceeds 24 hours.
  5. Do not ask the customer to replace the SIM or reset the handset.

title: Engineer missed installation appointment
body:
If the engineer did not arrive during the appointment window, apologise, check the job status for cancellations or access issues, and rebook the earliest slot with priority. Customers are entitled to a missed-appointment credit when the miss was the provider's fault.

  1. Check the job status to see why the visit did not happen: engineer delay, cancellation or failed access.
  2. Apologise and rebook the earliest available slot with priority flag.
  3. Offer the customer a morning or afternoon window and send SMS confirmation.
  4. Apply the missed appointment credit if the miss was the provider's fault.
  5. Escalate to the field operations supervisor if two appointments have been missed.

title: New connection not active after installation
body:
A new line that remains inactive after the engineer visit is usually waiting for final provisioning or was not activated on the exchange side. Check the order status; if the engineer closed the job but activation is pending, raise an expedited activation request. Provide the login credentials and confirm the activation date.

  1. Check the order status for pending provisioning or activation.
  2. If the engineer completed the job but activation is pending, raise an expedited activation request.
  3. Confirm the activation date and give the customer the router login credentials.
  4. Ask the customer to power-cycle the router once activation is confirmed.
  5. Escalate to provisioning support if activation is not complete within 24 hours.

title: Set-top box shows no picture or error code
body:
A TV with no picture from the set-top box is normally a cable, input or box provisioning problem. Check the HDMI cable and TV input, restart the box, and read the error code on screen. Error codes indicating authorisation loss need the box re-sent to the network to refresh entitlements.

  1. Check the HDMI cable and make sure the TV is on the correct input.
  2. Restart the set-top box by unplugging for one minute.
  3. Note the on-screen error code and check it against the error code list.
  4. Send a re-authorisation signal to the box to refresh entitlements.
  5. If the box still shows no picture, arrange a replacement box.

title: Evening disconnections - weekly line profile reset (superseded)
body: Customers whose broadband disconnects every evening should have their line profile reset to the default once a week. Ask them to leave the router off overnight.
